title: Crystal-Orientation-Dependent Image Contrast for Largely Defocused HAADF STEM Imaging
content: When imaging a bent nanoplatelet in Z-contrast STEM (Fig. 1A), a star-like structure can be observed when a large defocus is applied (Fig. 1B). The origin of this structure is uniquely related to the local crystallography of the platelet, namely the crystal orientation. For example, the crossing (arrow in Fig. 1B) marks an exact low-order zone axis orientation. In this work we provide a detailed explanation of bent contour contrast formation in defocused high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) STEM. To this end, we present 4D-STEM and STEM tomography experiments for a thin Bi2Te3-Sb2Te3 heteroparticle and ascribe the unique contrast features to enhanced or suppressed channeling via extensive multislice simulations [1].
